name: The Man Who Sold the World

podcast.body: Following the abrupt stoppage of "Station to Station" and a ten-minute break, David Bowie and his band returned to the stage in Prague on June 23, 2004, and played this song. "Then they went into the man who sold the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, written early in Bowie's career, describes an artist who achieves ultimate success but is met with disappointment, regretting the journey and ultimately feeling like a loser despite achieving his goals. The lyrical content, while not directly autobiographical for Bowie at the time of its composition, gained profound new meaning when covered by Curcomen, whose personal circumstances perfectly aligned with the song's narrative. "La canción de Menjusel de World que hizo Bowie es una canción en la rada en tercera persona de un artista que se canta si mismo que habla de si mismo."

podcast.body: This song was performed by Tony Visconti and Spiders from Mars drummer Woody Woodmansey as the band Holy Holy at a club in New York on January 8, 2016, Bowie's 69th birthday and the release day of *Blackstar*. Bowie was reportedly scheduled to appear but canceled at the last minute due to health, instead taking a phone call from the stage while the crowd sang "Happy Birthday" to him. "Tony Visconti and Spiders from Mars drummer Woody Woodman Z performed the man who sold the world at a club in New York under the name Holy Holy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
